title: Create a production test pipeline
prompt: Run linting, automated tests, and builds during continuous integration and prevent deployment on critical failure. Submit the relevant code or implementation notes and validate the complete behavior in a local Next.js project. CodeLeaf does not run arbitrary learner code; the configured grader is a bounded static marker check followed by review against the acceptance criteria.

starter.code:
npm ci
npm run lint
npm test
npm run build
starter.run_instructions: Adapt this starter in a local JavaScript/JSX App Router project. For server-side examples, provide the real data/auth helpers locally and use test credentials. Run focused tests and a production build; never include secrets or production data in a submission.

public_tests.name: Required concept markers
public_tests.description: A server-side static marker check confirms that the submission includes expected constructs. It does not prove complete functionality; review the listed acceptance criteria and exercise the application locally.

acceptance_criteria: The implementation meets the prompt requirements and uses the relevant Next.js convention.
Expected behavior can be reproduced with documented setup and test steps.
A meaningful empty, invalid, error, denied, or boundary case is tested.
Authorization and ownership are enforced in server-side code for protected operations.
The result is keyboard-usable, responsive, and understandable to users where UI is involved.
hints: Build a minimal working path first, then add the remaining acceptance criteria.
Record the expected output before testing and keep the test data synthetic.
A passing string-pattern check is not a substitute for a browser, integration, security, and production build review.
grading_method: Static pattern check only, followed by instructor/manual review for actual behavior, security, accessibility, and edge cases. This is not arbitrary-code execution or proof of correctness.
retry_policy: Retry is allowed. Incorrect submissions award no XP; the platform awards its fixed exercise XP only when its server-side configured check first succeeds, and only once per activity.
